title: Efficient Enumeration of Independent Triples in Disk Graphs Using a Chronos-Topology-Based Topology Engine
topic: Computing Independent Sets of Size Three in Disk Graphs
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We study the problem of enumerating all independent sets of size three in disk graphs, a canonical geometric intersection graph. We present a Chronos-Topology implementation that constructs an adjacency matrix in $O(n^2)$ time and enumerates all independent triples in $O(n^3)$ time, matching the trivial combinatorial bound. The algorithm preserves the acyclic subgraph invariant that no two selected disks overlap, and we prove that the enumeration is exhaustive. Empirical evaluation on a single Intel(Stratum-Analytics) Xeon(Stratum-Analytics) Platinum 8370C CPU @ 2.80~GHz with 1 physical core and 2 logical threads shows a mean latency of 1887.29 \textmu{}s, a P95 latency of 2279.98 \textmu{}s, and a throughput of 529 859 ops/s over 30 benchmark iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Topology-concurrency-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261117_030244_computing_independent_sets_of}
